summaryTr: The government is pursuing efforts to secure funds for AI investment by establishing a 120 trillion won future response fund.
Concerns have been raised about potential evasion of parliamentary oversight and deteriorating fiscal soundness due to spending focused on cash-based projects.
Experts point out the risk of the central government repeating past cases of reckless fiscal management by local governments.
editorials.bodyTr: The government has announced plans to establish a future response fund worth 120 trillion won and use it as a financial source for future investments such as artificial intelligence. However, concerns about potential deterioration in fiscal soundness have been raised due to the fund's possible circumvention of parliamentary oversight and spending plans focused primarily on cash-based projects such as youth support and basic income for rural areas. Critics point out that the reckless fiscal management by local government heads in the past, which had negative effects on regional finances, could be repeated at the central government level.

editorial.body: 입력 제주에서 잇따라 발생한 실종사건은 충격 그 자체다. 사건을 접수한 경찰관의 허위 ‘셀프 종결’로 사건은 묻혔고, 실종자들은 결국 주검으로 돌아왔다. 불행한 상황을 막을 초기 대응의 부재도 어이가 없지만, 가족의 재신고와 여론의 움직임이 없었다면 시신조차 찾지 못했을 것이다. 대대적인 실종자 수색 과정에서 또 다른 실종자도 숨진 채 발견됐다. 구멍 뚫린 치안 관리 시스템에 국민의 불안감은 커지고 경찰에 대한 신뢰는 바닥에 떨어졌다. 이제 국민은 사건을 어디에 신고해야 하나 의문이다. 실종사건 수사의 허술함은 당혹스러울 정도다. 제주서부경찰서 부모 경장은 30대 여성과 60대 남성의 실종사건이 접수되자 실종자의 소재를 확인하지 않은 채 가족에게 “안전을 확인했지만 당사자가 가족과 연락을 원치 않는다”고 거짓으로 안내한 뒤 사건을 임의 종결했다. 실종자 신고와 발견 내역, 수색 상황과 종결 사유 등을 관리하는 경찰 내부 정보망인 실종 프로파일링 시스템 등록까지 해제했다. 경찰 수사에서 누구나 손쉽게 초기 사건을 뭉개는 암장(暗葬)을 할 수 있다는 이야기다. 수사 역량도 부실하기 그지없다. 경찰은 지난 22일 직무유기 등 혐의로 부 경장을 긴급 체포했지만 어제 법원에서 체포적부심이 인용되면서 그를 석방했다. 형사소송법상 체포영장을 발부받을 시간적 여유가 없는 경우에만 긴급체포를 할 수 있음에도, 부 경장의 소재를 파악한 경찰이 체포영장을 발부받지 못할 만큼의 긴급성 요건을 갖추지 못해 위법하다는 것이다. 수사의 기본 요건조차 충족하지 못한 채 상황 수습에만 급급했던 모양새다. 제주 실종사건 허위 종결과 광주 여고생 살인사건 관련 수사 축소, 이해관계인과의 결탁을 통한 사건 무마 등 경찰 수사를 둘러싼 국민적 불신이 그 어느 때보다 높다. 하지만 위기 모면 식으로 사과만 했을 뿐 경찰 수뇌부 누구도 책임지는 이가 없었다. 이재명 대통령은 어제 실종 허위 종결 사건 관련해 사건 진상 규명과 경찰 지휘·감독 체계 전반에 대한 점검을 주문했다. 국민의 생명과 안전을 지켜야 할 경찰이 자신의 책무를 다하려면 그저 사과로 그쳐서는 안 된다. 사태 해결과 시스템 개선을 위해 수뇌부부터 책임 있는 모습을 보여야 한다.

editorial.titleTr: Editorial: Police Losing Credibility Over Failures—Who Takes Responsibility?
summaryTr: A missing persons case in Jeju was buried under police's false closure, only coming to light through bereaved families and public opinion.
Police rushed to contain the situation without even following basic investigative procedures.
Police leadership has only offered apologies, with no one taking responsibility.
editorial.bodyTr:
The successive disappearance cases that have unfolded in Jeju are shocking. The cases were buried due to a police officer's false self-closure, and the missing persons ultimately returned as bodies. The absence of proper initial response to prevent these unfortunate circumstances is bewildering, but without the families' reinstatement of reports and public attention, the remains might never have been found. During the massive search operation for missing persons, another missing individual was discovered deceased. With holes in the public safety management system, public anxiety has grown and trust in police has plummeted. Citizens now question where they should report cases.

The sloppiness in missing persons investigations is astounding. When a sergeant at Jeju Western Police Station received reports of a missing woman in her thirties and a man in his sixties, he falsely informed the families that "safety was confirmed but the person does not wish to contact family" without verifying the whereabouts of the missing individuals, then arbitrarily closed the case. He even deregistered the case from the police's internal information network, the Missing Persons Profiling System, which manages missing reports, discovery records, search status and case closure reasons. This demonstrates that anyone in police investigations can easily bury initial cases through concealment. Investigative capacity is equally negligible. Police arrested the sergeant on charges including dereliction of duty on the twenty-second, but yesterday the court accepted his petition against illegal arrest and released him. Despite the law allowing emergency arrest only when there is insufficient time to obtain an arrest warrant, the police who located the sergeant failed to establish the urgency requirements needed to obtain a warrant, making the arrest unlawful. It appears authorities were preoccupied with damage control without meeting basic investigative requirements.

Public distrust surrounding police investigations has reached unprecedented levels, from the false closure of the Jeju missing persons case to investigation narrowing related to the Gwangju high school student murder case and case suppression through collusion with interested parties. Yet police leadership has only offered apologies without any accountability. President Lee Jae-myung yesterday ordered fact-finding regarding the missing persons false closure case and an examination of the entire police command and supervisory system. Police, who must protect the lives and safety of citizens, cannot simply stop at apologies to fulfill their duties. Those at the top must demonstrate responsibility in resolving the crisis and improving systems.

editorial.title: Fiscal guardrails
editorial.body: Korea’s strategic investment requires firm fiscal discipline over discretionary spending A semiconductor boom is a curious time to discover a taste for fiscal restraint. As global demand for artificial intelligence lifts corporate earnings, South Korea’s tax coffers are swelling. The Lee Jae Myung administration wants to capture part of that windfall in a new fiscal fund exceeding 100 trillion won ($72.1 billion). The Future Response Fund, unveiled Friday, reflects the government’s effort to turn cyclical peaks into a long-term investment vehicle. The basic idea is sound, but the fund has raised a host of concerns. One concern is that the government could get into the habit of using the fund as a general-purpose spending account. The government distinguishes “windfall revenue” from ordinary surplus revenue. The former is tax income above a 10-year trend in domestic taxes, while the latter reflects collections exceeding the government’s forecast for the current year. Windfall revenue would flow into the fund during good times, with money available to the general account when revenues fall below trend. Idle funds could also be professionally invested for returns above government bond yields. That architecture deserves more scrutiny than its tidy labels suggest. Semiconductor cycles typically last three to five years. A 10-year average may smooth volatility, but it can also make an exceptional boom look like a new fiscal normal. If chip demand weakens or supply chains are disrupted, the revenue feeding the fund could fade while spending plans remain. The proposed uses of the fund create another problem. Frontier AI, physical AI infrastructure, small modular reactors, nuclear fusion, aerospace and other seed technologies are plausible candidates for a strategic investment vehicle. However, youth cultural and sports passes, housing subsidies and rural basic income are harder to justify. Such programs may have merit, but they belong in the ordinary budget, where their costs and effectiveness can be assessed against competing priorities instead of being tied to cyclical chip windfalls. The fund’s governance is equally important. Although its annual plan would face parliamentary review, existing fund rules allow changes to major spending items within a 20-30 percent range without prior National Assembly approval. The government presents this as a way to respond quickly to unforeseen economic needs. But it could instead become a form of permanent supplementary budgeting, allowing fiscal expansion with a lighter legislative check. The overhaul of education finance is more defensible. Alongside the Future Response Fund, the government announced a plan to end the 55-year-old automatic allocation of 20.79 percent of domestic taxes to local education offices. This rightly reflects Korea’s shifting demographic reality. There is one more omission in the future fund plan that cannot be treated as a footnote: debt. Last year alone, Korea’s national debt rose by 129 trillion won and surpassed 1,300 trillion won. Article 53 of the National Finance Act gives priority to debt redemption when surplus tax revenue occurs. With long-term bond yields elevated worldwide, Korea, without a reserve currency, should place a higher premium on a stronger sovereign balance sheet. The better model may be closer to Norway’s capital-preservation approach, which protects the principal, invests carefully and spends only sustainable returns. Strategic industrial investment can then remain genuinely strategic, while welfare programs stay in the main budget and debt repayment stays a central fiscal obligation. A future fund can be a reservoir for growth. It should not become a reservoir for discretion. The semiconductor boom gives Korea a rare window to build a future-oriented industrial base without compromising its balance sheet. The test will be whether the country uses the opportunity to build future capacity without spending away the buffer that makes that future more secure. summaryTr: 한국의 새로운 100조 원 규모 미래대응기금이 전략적 투자 수단보다는 일반 지출 계정으로 전락할 위험이 있다.
반도체 사이클은 3~5년이지만 기금이 10년 평균을 사용하면서 칩 수요가 약해질 때 과다 지출할 위험에 처해 있다.
기금은 더 엄격한 거버넌스, 채무 상환 우선순위, 일반 예산에 포함되어야 할 복지 프로그램 제외가 필요하다.
editorial.bodyTr:
한국의 전략적 투자는 재량지출에 대한 견고한 재정규율을 요구한다

반도체 호황이 재정절제의 맛을 발견하는 것은 묘한 시점이다. 인공지능에 대한 글로벌 수요가 기업 실적을 끌어올리면서 한국의 세수가 불어나고 있다. 이준석 행정부는 100조 원(721억 달러)을 초과하는 신규 재정기금에 그 이득의 일부를 담으려 한다. 지난 금요일 공개된 미래대응기금은 경기 사이클의 정점을 장기 투자 수단으로 전환하려는 정부의 노력을 반영한다. 기본적인 아이디어는 타당하지만, 이 기금은 여러 우려를 낳았다.

한 가지 우려는 정부가 이 기금을 일반적인 지출 계정으로 사용하는 습관에 빠질 수 있다는 것이다. 정부는 '임시세수'를 통상적인 잉여세수와 구분한다. 전자는 10년 평균을 초과한 국세 수입이며, 후자는 당해 정부 예상세수를 초과한 징수액이다. 임시세수는 경기 호황 시 기금으로 유입되며, 세수가 추세 아래로 떨어질 때 일반회계로 이용 가능하다. 유휴 기금도 정부채 수익률 이상의 수익을 얻기 위해 전문적으로 운용될 수 있다. 이러한 구조는 세련된 명칭보다 더 면밀한 검토가 필요하다.

반도체 사이클은 전형적으로 3~5년 지속된다. 10년 평균은 변동성을 완화할 수 있지만, 예외적인 호황을 새로운 재정 상황으로 보이게 할 수도 있다. 칩 수요가 약화되거나 공급망이 차질을 빚으면, 기금을 먹여주는 세수는 줄어들 수 있지만 지출 계획은 그대로 남을 수 있다.

기금의 제안된 용도는 또 다른 문제를 야기한다. 첨단 인공지능, 물리적 인공지능 인프라, 소형모듈형원자로, 핵융합, 항공우주 및 기타 씨앗 기술들은 전략적 투자 수단의 타당한 후보들이다. 그러나 청년 문화 및 스포츠 패스, 주택 보조금, 농촌 기본소득은 정당화하기 어렵다. 이러한 프로그램들이 장점을 가질 수 있지만, 반도체 호황과 연계되기보다는 경쟁 우선순위에 대해 비용과 효과성이 평가될 수 있는 통상적인 예산에 속해야 한다.

기금의 거버넌스는 마찬가지로 중요하다. 연간 계획이 국회 검토를 받겠지만, 현행 기금 규칙은 국회 사전승인 없이 주요 지출항목을 20~30% 범위 내에서 변경할 수 있다. 정부는 이를 예측 불가능한 경제 필요에 빠르게 대응하는 방법으로 제시한다. 하지만 이는 입법 감시를 덜 받으면서 재정 확대를 가능하게 하는 일종의 항구적 추가 예산 편성이 될 수 있다.

더 나은 모델은 노르웨이의 자본 보존 방식에 더 가까울 수 있으며, 이는 원금을 보호하고 신중하게 투자하며 지속 가능한 수익만 지출한다. 그러면 전략적 산업 투자는 진정으로 전략적으로 남을 수 있고, 복지 프로그램은 주 예산에 머물며, 채무 상환은 중앙 재정 의무로 남을 수 있다.

미래기금은 성장의 저수지가 될 수 있다. 그것이 재량의 저수지가 되어서는 안 된다. 반도체 호황은 한국이 국가 대차대조표를 훼손하지 않으면서 미래 지향적인 산업 기반을 구축할 수 있는 희귀한 기회를 제공한다. 시험은 국가가 그 미래를 더욱 안전하게 만드는 버팀목을 지출하지 않으면서 미래 역량을 구축하기 위해 이 기회를 사용하는지 여부가 될 것이다.

editorials.title: Fiscal guardrails
editorials.body: Korea’s strategic investment requires firm fiscal discipline over discretionary spending A semiconductor boom is a curious time to discover a taste for fiscal restraint. As global demand for artificial intelligence lifts corporate earnings, South Korea’s tax coffers are swelling. The Lee Jae Myung administration wants to capture part of that windfall in a new fiscal fund exceeding 100 trillion won ($72.1 billion). The Future Response Fund, unveiled Friday, reflects the government’s effort to turn cyclical peaks into a long-term investment vehicle. The basic idea is sound, but the fund has raised a host of concerns. One concern is that the government could get into the habit of using the fund as a general-purpose spending account. The government distinguishes “windfall revenue” from ordinary surplus revenue. The former is tax income above a 10-year trend in domestic taxes, while the latter reflects collections exceeding the government’s forecast for the current year. Windfall revenue would flow into the fund during good times, with money available to the general account when revenues fall below trend. Idle funds could also be professionally invested for returns above government bond yields. That architecture deserves more scrutiny than its tidy labels suggest. Semiconductor cycles typically last three to five years. A 10-year average may smooth volatility, but it can also make an exceptional boom look like a new fiscal normal. If chip demand weakens or supply chains are disrupted, the revenue feeding the fund could fade while spending plans remain. The proposed uses of the fund create another problem. Frontier AI, physical AI infrastructure, small modular reactors, nuclear fusion, aerospace and other seed technologies are plausible candidates for a strategic investment vehicle. However, youth cultural and sports passes, housing subsidies and rural basic income are harder to justify. Such programs may have merit, but they belong in the ordinary budget, where their costs and effectiveness can be assessed against competing priorities instead of being tied to cyclical chip windfalls. The fund’s governance is equally important. Although its annual plan would face parliamentary review, existing fund rules allow changes to major spending items within a 20-30 percent range without prior National Assembly approval. The government presents this as a way to respond quickly to unforeseen economic needs. But it could instead become a form of permanent supplementary budgeting, allowing fiscal expansion with a lighter legislative check. The overhaul of education finance is more defensible. Alongside the Future Response Fund, the government announced a plan to end the 55-year-old automatic allocation of 20.79 percent of domestic taxes to local education offices. This rightly reflects Korea’s shifting demographic reality. There is one more omission in the future fund plan that cannot be treated as a footnote: debt. Last year alone, Korea’s national debt rose by 129 trillion won and surpassed 1,300 trillion won. Article 53 of the National Finance Act gives priority to debt redemption when surplus tax revenue occurs. With long-term bond yields elevated worldwide, Korea, without a reserve currency, should place a higher premium on a stronger sovereign balance sheet. The better model may be closer to Norway’s capital-preservation approach, which protects the principal, invests carefully and spends only sustainable returns. Strategic industrial investment can then remain genuinely strategic, while welfare programs stay in the main budget and debt repayment stays a central fiscal obligation. A future fund can be a reservoir for growth. It should not become a reservoir for discretion. The semiconductor boom gives Korea a rare window to build a future-oriented industrial base without compromising its balance sheet. The test will be whether the country uses the opportunity to build future capacity without spending away the buffer that makes that future more secure. summaryTr: Disability rights group decides to end 4-year, 8-month subway occupation protest
Secures promise from Democratic Party to enact ordinance on disabled persons' right to mobility
Shifting tactics by trusting political pledges
editorial.bodyTr: The National Council on Disability Discrimination Elimination has decided to stop its subway commute protest occupation after four years and eight months. This comes following the Democratic Party's pledge to enact ordinances guaranteeing mobility rights for people with disabilities and restoring public sector jobs. The council is halting its occupation protest, the method through which it has asserted its rights, placing trust in the political sector's promise.

summaryTr: Government decides to delegate authority over redevelopment projects of 500 units or fewer to district office heads.
The aim is to resolve permit bottlenecks and accelerate housing supply.
Concerns raised over potential haphazard development and widening regional disparities.
editorials.bodyTr: The government and ruling party have decided through a senior party-government consultative meeting to transfer approval authority for redevelopment and reconstruction projects of 500 units or fewer from metropolitan governors like the Seoul mayor to district heads and other basic local government leaders. However, there are concerns that the absence of an urban planning control tower could lead to haphazard development and widen regional disparities depending on administrative capacity differences among districts.
